t: Nothing of St Martin Vintry stands today. It was a parish church in the Vintry ward of the City of London, destroyed in the Great Fire of 1666 and never rebuilt. Two notable people were buried here. Sir Richard Lyons was a merchant who held a monopoly on selling sweet wine in London, until the Good Parliament impeached him in 1376. He was a sheriff of London and a member of parliament, and Wat Tyler killed him during the Peasants' Revolt. Sir Cuthbert Hacket, also a merchant, was Lord Mayor of London in 1626.
